text:
maria: FYI I'm hitting a reproducible JSON.parse error in the JS sample app when a long SSE stream crosses an auth refresh. Repro steps below.

sam: Interesting. Hosted/staging or dedicated?

maria: Hosted (staging). JS SDK 2.3.1, Next sample app, EventSource polyfill. If I force token refresh ~30s into a stream the client sometimes logs parse errors.

kevin: Do you have raw SSE frames? My suspicion is that two sockets overlap during reconnect and events interleave.

maria: Minimal capture (trimmed):

[data] data: {"id":"a1","part":"hello wo"
[data] data: {"id":"a1","part":"rld"}
[data] data: {"id":"a2","part":"next"}

But when refresh occurs I sometimes see: 
[data] data: {"id":"a1","part":"hello "
[data] data: {"id":"a2","part":"next"}
[data] data: {"id":"a1","part":"world"}

The SDK emits msg a2 then a broken a1 fragment which causes JSON.parse to throw.

yuki: Do we include resume token / last-event-id on reconnect? We added resume-token recently.

maria: Server does send resume-token but the polyfill opens a new ES connection while the old socket is still closing (seen ~150-250ms overlap). The polyfill forwards messages from both sockets immediately, so ordering can get scrambled. Also saw a cached chunk replay + new chunk concatenated then parsed.

sam: So there are two problem vectors: (1) overlap/reconnect races, (2) client parse logic that doesn't handle fragment reassembly. Short-term workaround is to ensure client waits for close before opening new EventSource on token refresh. Long-term fix is server-side fragment sequencing and client reassembly logic.

maria: I pushed a quick change to the sample app to wait for the old ES instance to emit 'close' before creating a new one. That eliminated the local repro for me. But some users on staging still hit it, probably due to differences in polyfill behavior or network timing.

sasha: Could we add a tiny marker in each SSE data envelope like "frag_seq" + a stream-level "msg_id" so clients can order fragments deterministically?

yuki: Yes, proposal: server adds "frag_seq" and preserves last_event_id across reconnects. SDKs should buffer partial fragments and only JSON.parse when a complete fragment sequence is available or when a gap is detected and reconciliation succeeds. Add unit tests that simulate reordering and partial chunks.

kevin: I'll create a network proxy test to inject 0-500ms overlaps and random reordering to validate the fixes. Also add telemetry event when parse errors occur with resume-token and socket ids to triage.

stream-bot: INFO: deploy-log: sample-app build with SSE debug logging deployed to staging.

maria: Filed issues: devex#448 (js-sdk close-before-open guard), infra#227 (sse frag_seq header + resume semantics), e2e#121 (auth-overlap harness). I'll link PRs shortly.

sam: For docs: add a short note in SDK onboarding: "If you plan to refresh tokens mid-stream, ensure the client waits for the SSE connection to close or use server-side fragment_seq/resume semantics."

yuki: I'll add SDK tests that feed partial JSON strings and out-of-order fragments to the parser to ensure it buffers correctly. Also add a spec for how resume-token and frag_seq interact.

maria: Thanks everyone. Follow-up PRs incoming and I'll update the sample-app changelog. :thumbsup:
